notes: Web 432 — NAV-CAMERA-JITTER (Nov 12, 2026; layers on web 431). The owner's film, Nov 12 10:43 CST, stopped at the 80 Avenue NE site entrance: the paste-a-link flow WORKED (routing started, 8.0 km), but in the drive view the camera would not sit still — the satellite view zoomed far out and crept back, the view drifted off the truck until the 🎯 Back to my truck pill stood on screen, the next-turn distance counted 30 -> 20 -> 10 m on a truck reading 0 km/h, an 'Off route' fired and re-routed him where he sat, and the route line flipped colour on the new plan. THE FIX (modules/navigator.js only) is a standstill judge plus a camera lock. (1) STANDSTILL (NAVPURE standstillStep, stepped on every fix in onPos): a 2.5 s spell of fixes that never stray more than 20 m from the spell's first fix and end within 8 m of it proves the truck parked (a spell a truck merely passing through can never complete — at 5 m/s the window's end fix sits 12.5 m out, at 10 m/s 25 m); that first fix becomes the ANCHOR, and the proof then holds until a fix leaves the wider 35 m disc. Guidance reads the believed position/speed (navPos/navSpeed): trackProgress, paintStep and the drive tick project the ANCHOR, so the countdown, maneuver index and arrival hold still with the truck; a proven standstill never enters the off-route block and never wears the reroute pill; the believed heading FREEZES in onPos (standstill wander mints random >=10 m derived bearings — chasing them rotated the parked view); the parked-arrival gate reads the believed speed, so a stale moving-fix speed cannot veto a real park. Reported speed never enters the judgement — position is the ground truth; a genuine crawl leaves the disc by travel alone (honest bound: guidance can lag a within-disc crawl by at most the disc's width). (2) CAMERA LOCK: while follow owns the view, the zoom is the FOLLOW ZOOM — recorded when the drive opens (18) and moved afterwards ONLY by the driver's own pinch (gesturePinchZoom re-records it). A foreign zoom no longer stands the follow down (the v215 zoomstart hook did exactly that: camera surrendered, pill up, nothing brought the truck back); it is corrected back around the follow target at zoomend, with the tick's zoom lock as backstop. The animator's glide advances from the believed position at the believed speed — parked, the aim IS the anchor and the animator's keep-alive sleeps; the tick's plane repaint and the animator's heading ease are gated on the same proof, so the parked view cannot slowly rotate. A driver's own DRAG still enters free-look exactly as before, and the 🎯 pill still hands the view back. UNTOUCHED: Navigate from pin (v430), the PiP strip (v427), the GPS voice (v428), dispatch-notes pins (v429), the Documents page (v431), routing, counting. Bench: the new suite tools/nav-camera-still-v432-test.js replays the filmed stop (a stationary jitter trace at a route waypoint: no countdown movement, no off-route, no re-route, follow target constant, glide aim constant) and a moving drive (still never proves, projection advances with travel, the follow zoom changes only through the pinch writer); A/B against pristine 431 bytes and the nav regression set are reported in the ship record. VERDICT OWED IN HIS HANDS: his next drive — parked, the view must sit on the truck and the distance must hold; moving, the camera must stay locked at the follow zoom on the truck. Not claimed until he drives it.
